content:
Marking the end of the Lean FRO's second year, we have a fantastic new release for you: v4.22.0-rc2.

Please see the release notes for full details.

As usual Mathlib, doc-gen4, verso, Batteries, Aesop, and the REPL are available using this toolchain using the v4.22.0-rc2 tag at the respective repositories (and ProofWidgets at v0.0.66). We encourage all projects downstream of these to update when possible (and to release their own v4.22.0-rc2 after updating).

Here are some highlights from this release:

  • A new Lean-native SMT-style tactic grind, along with annotations for the Lean standard library. Here's a quick demo. grind ships theory specific solvers already including cutsat (superseding omega, with model construction) and a new Grobner basis solver. There is a new chapter in the Lean Language Reference explaining how to use grind.
  • The old compiler has been replaced by the new compiler! (lean#8577) This already closes many old issues, and lays the foundation for many future feature and performance improvements.
  • lake new MyProject math now generates a template that include doc-gen4,and an automatic update workflow (lean#8866). Also auto-implicits are now enabled by default in this template.
  • User interface improvements, giving pop-up help: completing a function call and displaying the import hierarchy
  • Optimized iterators for many data types in the Lean Standard Library.

This release also has some experimental features which are not intended for general use yet, but daring early adopters can start exploring and giving feedback. Expect rough edges, feature incompleteness, and minimal documentation here!

  • the new module sytem, enabled by the module keyword before import statements
  • the new monadic verification framework (lean#8995)
  • sharing oleans between different checkouts of the same repository (lean#8922; requires export LAKE_ARTIFACT_CACHE=true for now)
  • polymorphic ranges and slices
Discussion about this release at #general > v4.22.0-rc2

Small announcement: we've decided to shift the release cycle (for both release candidates and stable releases) so these happen mid-month rather than end-of-month. This better suits our internal processes at the FRO.

In particular, this means that v4.22.0 and v4.23.0-rc1 won't be coming out this week, and will wait until mid-August.
